ArXiv cs.AI.title: SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is usually benchmarked by one heart rate per video, a figure that hides the short windows in which a tele-consultation would actually read the pulse. We present SAMA, a training-free estimator that (i) forms a quality-weighted consensus of POS and CHROM chrominance spectra, (ii) discounts frequencies occupied by pulse-free references derived from the same frames (frame motion, skin-mask geometry and background brightness), (iii) follows the heart rate through time with a Viterbi ridge under a random-walk prior,

ArXiv cs.AI.title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28195v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Tsetlin machine learns propositional rules with teams of Tsetlin automata that are driven by reward and penalty rather than gradients, so its models are interpretable by construction and cheap to evaluate. Its software, however, consists of C and CUDA kernels behind scikit-learn-style wrappers that sit outside the deep learning ecosystem. torchtsetlin implements the Tsetlin machine family as ordinary PyTorch modules: vanilla and weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional over sequences, images and volumes, and dense per-pixel segmentatio

ArXiv cs.AI.title: From Point Clouds to Engineering Models: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents can translate 3D measurements into CAD geometry, but reconstructing engineering models for the built environment demands semantic interpretation and consistent construction constraints beyond surface fitting. We formulate scene-level Scan-to-BIM (Building Information Modeling) as an agentic 3D coding task and introduce S2Bench, comprising public and proprietary scans of 128 real-world scenes across five domains, paired with expert-curated reference models spanning diverse spatial scales. A shared framework lets agents measure scans

ArXiv cs.AI.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28202v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an o

ArXiv cs.AI.title: FinEvo: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Financial Modeling
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28239v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have expanded their role in high-value productivity tasks, including financial analysis and modeling, while enabling models to play an increasingly active role in their own improvement. This motivates two complementary lines of inquiry: can financial modeling capabilities provide a foundation for model self-evolution, and can self-evolution, in turn, advance financial capabilities? We introduce FinEvo, a self-evolution framework that integrates autonomous experience construction with financial capability

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it store

ArXiv cs.AI.title: A Nepali-Accented English Evaluation Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28263v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems perform strongly on native-English benchmarks, yet their accuracy degrades sharply when the input speech comes from under represented non-native accents. Nepali-accented English is particularly under-served: existing resources either focus on native Nepali speech, cover broader multi-accent settings without dedicated Nepali evaluation, or provide only limited Nepali-accent coverage. This paper presents a Nepali-accented English evaluation dataset designed to support robust ASR benchmarking under accent

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Temporal Logic Tensor Networks: Foundations of Temporal Reasoning in Neural Networks
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In dynamic scenes---football matches, traffic streams, surgery, or assembly---actions unfold at fundamentally different time scales: in football, a kick happens in milliseconds, a possession lasts seconds, and complex events such as a successful pass followed by a goal combine multiple atomic actions over extended durations. Models trained solely on visual data struggle to learn effectively across different time scales, lacking a principled way of reasoning across fine-grained instants and broader intervals. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Specialized Large Language Models for Markovian Reasoning: Structural Cache Compression, Transition Pretraining, and Dual-Loop Transformers
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Standard autoregressive large language models attend to the growing history of generated tokens, making the key-value (KV) cache a central memory and throughput bottleneck in long-chain reasoning and multi-branch sampling. Yet an important class of reasoning problems is naturally first-order Markovian: the next step depends on a sufficient representation of the current state, rather than on the raw sequence of all earlier steps. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Feedback-Driven Prompt Refinement for Educational AI: Affective Trajectory Estimation and Bloom's Taxonomy Classification
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28293v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Contribution: This study has shown that a shared prompt-refinement procedure, guided by distinct affective and cognitive feedback signals, can improve held-out reference agreement and multi-label classification while reducing affective-generation variability without executor parameter updates. Background: Industry 4.0 has increased demand for personalized technical education across interconnected computing and engineering domains, while prompt sensitivity and generation variability have complicated dependable interpretation of instructional dial

ArXiv cs.AI.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28295v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scientific information extraction (IE) is a fundamental component of AI for Science, transforming experimental knowledge embedded in scientific literature into structured and traceable data for evidence synthesis, scientific database construction, and data-driven discovery. However, critical experimental details are often distributed across text, tables, figures, captions, and surrounding discussion, making them difficult to recover using conventional text-only extraction. Existing LLM-based and multimodal RAG pipelines typically rely on full-do

ArXiv cs.AI.title: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28314v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Abliteration is a widely used white-box attack against the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs). It elicits harmful behavior by estimating a refusal direction in the model's activation space and projecting that direction out of the residual-stream write-out matrices. We propose INSEP, a defense that fine-tunes the model to reduce the separability of harmful and benign activations along the refusal direction. Abliteration estimates this direction as a difference in class means and projects it out. Reducing separability weakens the sig

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Selection Policies for Equal-Byte Mixed-Precision Quantization of Small Language Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28318v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can changing which matrices receive 2, 4, or 8 bits improve a small language model without increasing its parameter storage? I compare two parent-selection rules in the same genetic algorithm: a binary-tournament variant and an Alternis-inspired rule. A separate baseline samples repaired random allocations without crossover or mutation. All three use the same MLX affine quantizer, byte ceiling, initialization and candidate allowance within each study. An exploratory study on Qwen3.5-2B evaluates 90 allocations per run. The main study on Qwen3-1.

ArXiv cs.AI.title: MatHarness: Towards Long-Horizon Open-ended AutoResearch for Computational Materials Science
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28324v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Materials science research is a non-linear, long-horizon process. Existing scientific agents, however, largely rely on specific task execution or predefined workflows, rendering them brittle in open-ended settings. To bridge this gap, we present MatHarness, an agent harness designed for open-ended, long-horizon computational materials research spanning the complete lifecycle from initial ideation to manuscript writing. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Decision models for UAVBench and the viability of edge deployment
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.28331v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Small language models are often proposed for reasoning onboard a drone.
